title: QWEN38-MTP flags from the recipe
verdict: The MTP flag is present in the build (`--spec-type draft-mtp` in build129), but there's nothing to test it on: the only Qwen3.8-27B on disk is a third-party quantum `pxqn-onecard` (13.57 GB), its tensor type 263 is outside the list of llama.cpp (0..44), and the engine fails to load in 0.33s (`failed to read tensor info`, rc=1) before flag parsing even begins. Both base and MTP configurations died the same way. There's no native GGUF for this model; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is only available in Strata shards (IQ1_M 58 GB, UD-IQ4_XS 93.7 GB), which can't be loaded in one pass on a 16 GB card. The claimed +33-39% decode boost on our card remains untested: there's no artifact that the engine accepts.

title: Xing4.0-29B-A4B in IQ2_M
verdict: Negative. The 2-bit quant does what it promises on memory - a 29B MoE resident in 16 GB at 71 tok/s decode - but code quality lands at 0.425, below the card's 0.55 bar and below even a 7B model at Q8_0 (0.625) and a 7B in 4-bit AWQ (0.50). Worth keeping only as a fast drafter or summarizer, not as a coding model.

title: v100-llm-kit: prebuilt SM70 binaries vs our own build
verdict: Mixed: prefill 16 % faster with the shipped sm_70 binaries, decode identical. Worth taking for long prompts (document analysis, repository context); not a reason to migrate a decode-bound workload. The vendor's agent wrapper (`serve-qwen3.sh`, Claude Code integration) and the claimed Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT Q4_0 in 16 GB were not tested.

title: Marlin_v100: INT4-cores Marlin on sm_70
verdict: Workspace assembled: BUILD_RC=0 in 3368 s (56 min), `_C.abi3.so` 509 MB and `_moe_C.abi3.so` 447 MB, loading on sm_70, `torch.ops._C.marlin_gemm` in place. Dense class matrix: 12/12 cases OK, `max_abs=0`, MISMATCH=0. Core speed flat: 175–185 µs at M from 1 to 5120 (K=512, N=256), i.e., limited by fixed overhead, not count; max 7.28 TFLOP/s at M=5120. Baseline on same shapes, torch fp16 (cuBLAS): 17.4 µs at M=1, 18.3 at M=512, 25.9 at M=4096 (41.5 TF/s), 27.5 at M=5120 (48.8 TF/s). Verdict: **negative** - Marlin path on sm_70 is 7–10x slower than regular fp16 GEMM; decoding not accelerated, at M=1 core spends 178 µs where cuBLAS spends 17. "Plus 20% to decode on GPTQ/AWQ" criterion not met; reason visible at core level - Volta INT4 path doesn't get tensor cores MMA-type or cp.async, and each call pays fixed price.

title: colibri: a three-tier expert engine, slower than llama.cpp here
verdict: The engine builds and runs on Volta: the server holds **8 529 MiB**, resident weights load in 5.2 s, and decode lands at **16.2 and 16.6 tok/s** on the two warm runs (mean over three runs 12.9). That is **4.5x below** our 75.5 tok/s record for the same model shape. Two blockers worth recording, because they cost most of the time here: - colibri does not read GGUF at all - it wants `config.json` plus safetensors shards, so the 19 GB GGUF we already had could not be used and the model had to be installed from its catalog; - supported families are frontier MoE architectures (deepseek_v4, glm, lfm3, qwen3-moe); `qwen2` is rejected with `unsupported model_type`.

title: FlashQLA-SM70: Gated DeltaNet
verdict: The V100 core executes and is accurate with a maximum deviation from the reference cycle of 0.0 on the form 1x512x2hx4kvxd128, time 0.5 ms compared to 575 ms for the Python cycle (1099x - against the cycle, not against the optimized baseline), VRAM 15 MiB. The card criterion (throughput gain of 25% on the hybrid model) cannot be verified: neither llama.cpp nor Strata invoke this operator. The high-level API still fails on sm_70: two guards `sm90 only` are bypassed manually.

title: Fused dequant of quantized KV
verdict: A/B on one model (27B IQ3_S, 10.95 GiB, fits entirely) and the same flags (`-p 8192 -n 8 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -r 1`): base build129 gives **799.82** TOPS prefilling, PR #31802 (HEAD 01eb64f, built under sm_70 with `GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=OFF`) - **599.35**. That is, prefilling **drops by 25 %**, decoding does not change (35.18 vs 35.10). The card's criterion was +15 % prefilling - failed with the opposite sign. Separately: the PR tree takes around 90 minutes to build (fattn instances), three attempts, successful - with unnecessary quant FA turned off. Verdict: **Negative for Volta** - unpacked KV on sm_70 is slower, not faster. Most likely reason: PR's win lives in tensor cores MMA, and V100 goes to vector core where extra branch only adds work. Reopen the card if PRs behave differently. **Result type.** Negative. **Does not show.** No profiling attribution: drop measured but not broken down by counters. Only pp8192 checked - 16k model with q8_0 KV no longer fits with prefilling buffers; had to abandon 30B MoE config from V100-51, model didn't load on that context.

title: Images on 4060 Ti, code on V100
verdict: Mixed: the 4060 Ti reaches 1885 images per hour on the turbo preset and 519 at 30 steps, but it is slower than the V100 in all three modes, so moving the factory would not speed generation up. Its real value is different - it produces 519-1885 images per hour without occupying the V100, which is what the queue lost six hours of code time to.

title: What a 4060 Ti can do that a V100 cannot
verdict: Mixed: the desktop card pre-fills faster at mid context and equals the V100 at 8.5k tokens, but decodes 1.9x slower, so no tested task finishes sooner on it. Inference stays on the V100; the desktop card is useful only where Volta lacks the hardware - and that is a diffusion/bf16 question, not a tokens-per-second question.

title: Batch half-and-half: 20 tasks for both cards
verdict: Criterion 1.5x passed only on 14B: distributing 12 tasks on V100 and 8 on PC yields 1.53x compared to one V100 (20.46 → 13.38 s, n=3), on 7B it's 1.43x (10.62 → 7.43 s, n=2). Quality remained unchanged: the set of accepted tasks matched the single-machine run (11/20 for 14B, 15/20 for 7B). The speed ratio sets the ceiling: PC delivers 0.58 of V100's speed (1.60 vs 0.93 s per task), thus a second machine doesn't provide more ~1.6x with any split, and distributing 13/7 is worse (1.40x) - PC is the bottleneck.

title: Llama.cpp RPC: one model on two cards
verdict: 27.11.2026, llama.cpp b12811 (00d5c142c, ready binaries ubuntu-cuda-12.8), Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M 17.28 GB (does not fit in 16 GB of one card). Split V100 + 4060 Ti via `--rpc` (`-dev CUDA0/RPC0 -ts 0.50/0.50`): pp512 **2405 ± 136 tok/s**, tg128 **54.9 ± 3.7 tok/s** (n=3). Base line - same model on one V100 only way possible, `-ncmoe 8` (experts 8 layers in RAM): pp512 **1181 ± 36**, tg128 **77.9 ± 12.6 tok/s** (n=3). Conclusion: pool of two cards gives ×2.0 prefill, but decode is 29% slower than CPU experts on one card; channel 106 MB/s not bottleneck for decode - eaten by RPC overhead per layer.

title: Prompt-expander: LLM writes prompt for photographer
verdict: The hypothesis was partially confirmed, and the solution depends on the prompt length. 20 product positions via vikhr-nemo-12b: valid JSON 20/20, all three keys 20/20, English without Cyrillic 20/20, 2.52 seconds per position on average (first 16.5s - cold load), 98-131 output tokens (was 124-189 in prototype). Visual spot-check on 5 positions (RealVisXL V5, 832x1216, 30 steps): long prompt 27-36 words gave 3/5 for material and color (vase and eustoma disappeared, pot lost packaging), short prompt in fixed order (16-22 words, 53-67 tokens) - 5/5. Packaging-box in frame 1 out of 5: SDXL draws the product, not the packaging, and ask for box separately.

title: background-swap-three-methods
verdict: Positive for the catalogue path: the deterministic white background wins on untouchable product pixels and cost, while img2img and inpainting stay for interior scenes where a prompt cannot steer colour reliably. Three methods, three clear roles, no method pretending to do all three.

verdict: Feedback is not the bottleneck: 0 of 8 with four iterations each, every patch syntactically valid and every one wrong, because the fixes need coordinated changes across files that the loop never allows.

title: inkling-2-mini-loop-cycles
verdict: Reasoning depth does not pay for short tasks: pass@1 stays flat at 0.475-0.525 across all three levels (spread ±0.15 at 95 %), while the high level doubles mean time per task (36.7 s vs 17.1 s). Decode speed is unchanged at 34 tok/s. ## Configuration `Inkling-2-Mini-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf`, 13.63 GB, 26.4 B parameters with 3.4 B active, 128 experts with 8 per token. llama.cpp master build129, `-ngl 99 -c 8192 --jinja`, three `--reasoning-effort` levels. The model fits entirely: **15 033 MiB** of 16 144 used, leaving almost nothing for context — 8192 tokens fit, 16k on the same card would not. ## Numbers 40 MBPP tasks per level, single run, acceptance by running the tests: | Level | pass@1 | Mean time | Mean answer | tok/s | Truncated by cap | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | none | 0.500 (20/40) | 17.1 s | 583 tok | 34.1 | 5 of 40 | | medium | **0.525** (21/40) | 18.3 s | 623 tok | 34.1 | 7 of 40 | | high | 0.475 (19/40) | 36.7 s | 1240 tok | 33.8 | 8 of 40 | At 40 tasks and p≈0.5 the spread is about ±0.15 at 95 %, so all three rows are statistically indistinguishable. Medium beat none by one task; high trailed by one and cost twice as much. Decode speed is identical across levels (33.8-34.1 tok/s): the loop core neither speeds up nor slows down with reasoning depth, only answer length grows. ## The trap that made the first measurement wrong The first high run used a 1400-token cap and reported 0.375 (15/40). That would have been read as "high level is worse", but 13 of 40 answers hit exactly 1400 — the model never got to write code after its reasoning. A rerun with a 3000 cap gave 0.475. A 10-point gap on the same level is the price of the cap, not of the model. Rule stands: for reasoning models, count truncated answers before looking at pass@1. ## What it means for the contour For this class of task (short MBPP functions) reasoning depth is not needed: 34 tok/s and 0.5 pass@1 on none, in half the time per task. High only pays where the task needs a long chain — and on our hardware a 27B model with an external plan (Ternary-Bonsai) gives 0.55 at 67 tok/s in 6.8 GB instead of 15. So Inkling is interesting not for MBPP quality but because 26.4 B parameters fit into 16 GB at Q3_K_XL with solid Russian text and agent-style answers. For an agentic contour it is a workable option, with one caveat: the model occupies 15 GB, so nothing else runs on the card alongside it. ## What these numbers do not prove - That the levels are equivalent on long tasks: MBPP is short functions where reasoning is barely needed. - That 0.475-0.525 is the model's ceiling: only levels were compared, no external models on the same 40 tasks. - That high does not help in agentic scenarios: different task type, untested. - That Q3_K_XL holds quality versus Q2: single quantisation. ## Reproduction ``` ssh the GPU guest /home/hermes/venvs/cu121/bin/python mbpp_inkling.py none medium high # 1400 cap MAXTOK=3000 /home/hermes/venvs/cu121/bin/python mbpp_inkling.py high # 3000 cap ``` Raw data: `/srv/media/night/v144_{none,medium,high}_40.json`, summary `v144_summary_40.json`, logs `/srv/media/night/mbpp_inkling*.log`.

title: lora-monstera-no-benefit
verdict: Training ran to completion on 30 monstera images and changed nothing visible in the product shots, so this LoRA is not worth keeping; the same budget is better spent on reference images per SKU than on a brand-wide adapter.

title: nemotron-bolt-e4b-fast-honest
verdict: Positive with a caveat: the model reaches 113 tok/s and answers honestly on the tested questions, so it qualifies as the fast working model; SenseNova is blocked outright by the engine.

title: olala-mini-unblocked-slow
verdict: Negative against the card's own bar: the model can be made to run on the fork, but the throughput it reaches is far below the 140 tok/s criterion, so the MoE shape bought memory headroom rather than speed.

title: print-from-640-library
verdict: A4 at 310 dpi is print-ready after one x4 pass at 0.7 s per card; A3 is not (219 dpi) and needs a second tiled ESRGAN pass, which doubles sharpness on the same output size but costs about a hundred times more time.

title: product-background-swap
verdict: Backgrounds can be replaced, the product cannot: product SSIM reaches 0.851 with depth conditioning while contour SSIM stays at 0.701, and the eye confirms redrawn petals and centres. Product cards need a manual cutout over a generated background.

title: rag-nemotron-vs-vikhr
verdict: Negative for the RAG role: Nemotron is twice as fast but three times more often wrong against the local vikhr model, so for customer-facing retrieval it loses on accuracy.

title: shop-assistant-similar-products
verdict: Retrieval is fine and first choice is not: the right variant is in the top five 90 % of the time but first only 15 %, so the assistant must list the varieties instead of picking one, which is now enforced in the system prompt.

title: ternary-bonsai-27b
verdict: Mixed: the ternary 27B does run here and holds 6.8 GB, but the throughput it reaches decides whether the trade is worth it for the shop - see the measurement above.

title: Upscaling for print: ESRGAN vs UltraSharp, SUPIR blocked by the channel
verdict: | Method | Time | Peak VRAM | Sharpness at 2560 | delta-E mean | delta-E max | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | LANCZOS (base) | 0,1 s | - | - | - | - | | Real-ESRGAN x4plus | 0,9 s | 2 722 MiB | 5,5 | 3,9 | 6,1 | | 4x-UltraSharp | 0,7 s | 2 722 MiB | 15,5 | 4,9 | 7,4 | The source measured 22,5 on the same Laplacian; the sharpness values are comparable only within the "at 2560" column, because upscaling changes the noise scale. The card's colour threshold was delta-E <= 3 and neither GAN passed (3,9 and 4,9), so even the mild upscaler cannot go to print without colour correction. What the 1:1 crop shows: LANCZOS keeps no hairs and smears petals into patches. Real-ESRGAN gains contrast and separates some petals, but leaves waxy regions, blotchiness and over-sharpened edges, and still does not recover individual hairs - it predicts plausible texture rather than returning the real one. 4x-UltraSharp is three times sharper, and that is exactly where generation traces appear: a blocky peach-and-white shape that does not exist in the scene, white specks, brush strokes in the brown areas, scales turned into smears. SUPIR did not run: 1,75 GB of the checkpoint is missing (5 329 810 432 bytes expected, 3 580 401 865 on disk - a zip without a central directory, which torch refuses), and the channel could not deliver it. Hugging Face served 4-5 KB/s with four parallel streams totalling 19 KB/s, the local proxy answered `Network is unreachable`, and GitHub releases were throttled to 26 B/s, while Cloudflare on the same machine gave 25,4 MB/s.

title: video-cogvideox-blocked
verdict: With cuDNN 9 video is blocked for a build reason, not a model limit: fp16 convolutions find no engine on sm_70, and without cuDNN the VAE asks 17.8 GiB. The fix is a cuDNN 8 environment, measured in V100-141, not a smaller clip.

title: vlm-card-controller-fails
verdict: Negative: the 3B VLM accepted every card it was shown, good and bad alike, so as a controller it carries no signal - a human or a mechanical check still has to do the deciding.
